datasets: 'Gun Trace Task Force settlements' (claimed Open Baltimore; actually 3 synthetic rows, dataset does not exist on Open Baltimore)
'BPD GIS incidents' with officer_id/shift/unit columns (claimed Open Baltimore; actually 3 synthetic rows, no such schema exists)
concurrency_primitives: rayon::join for the two CSV loads (ingestion.rs:78-81); rayon par_iter().map().collect() over settlements in the join (pipeline.rs:24-39 via concurrency.rs:5-10); single tokio spawn_blocking task wrapping the whole pipeline (main.rs:41-53); analyses sequential
design_patterns: Builder (QueryConfig::builder().district().build()), Strategy (trait AnalysisStrategy with 5 unit-struct implementors via &dyn), explicit pipeline in main; zero-copy borrowed JoinedRecord<'a>
questions: Q1 Settlement cost by district alongside incident counts
Q2 Units/shifts in officer_id-matched settlement-incident pairs
Q3 Misconduct reports vs disciplinary actions per year (settlements only)
Q4 Recurring officer identifiers across both files with cost vs mean
Q5 District risk index = 0.6*normalized cost + 0.4*normalized incidents
overview: Idiomatic Rust split into seven small modules with a real Builder, a Strategy trait dispatched via &dyn, clap CLI, anyhow errors, and a zero-copy borrowed join; compiles warning-free. No tests, a 10-line rayon wrapper and a tokio runtime used for a single blocking task pad out the concurrency story, serde_json is unused, and the companion index.html dashboard renders hard-coded mock numbers rather than program output. README reads as generated marketing copy and is truncated.
stakeholder_value: None in practice: the data is six invented rows about a dataset Open Baltimore does not publish, so every answer (Western district costs $200K, OFF-001 recurs) is fiction, and the dashboard shows an 'Eastern District' and 'OFF-042' that the engine never computed. Only Q2 is a genuine cross-dataset join; the others are side-by-side single-dataset counts. The misconduct-liability theme would be interesting with real settlement data, but the officer-level incident schema it assumes is not public.
issues: Fully synthetic data: 3+3 rows with John Doe/Jane Smith/OFF-001; claimed 'GTTF settlements' and officer-linked incidents are not Open Baltimore datasets; README's 'official Open Baltimore datasets' claim is false
No path to real data: URL flags expect the same invented schema; no generator; no source URLs
README has no macOS build/execute/verify instructions and is truncated mid code block; only run.sh documents the build
192 MB target/ directory (989 build-artifact files incl. 7.3 MB debug binary from nightly rustc 1.99) committed and shipped; shipped binary is SIGKILLed on launch; no .gitignore
index.html dashboard is static mockData unconnected to the Rust program, with districts/officers that exist nowhere else
Token concurrency: rayon::join of two loads + par_iter over three rows; analyses sequential; tokio runtime wraps one spawn_blocking
No tests; unused serde_json dependency; empty data/data/ directory; .vscode/ shipped
Q1 bar chart renders $75K and $200K as identical full-width bars (sqrt + clamp)
rationale: Full build credit and a reasonable architecture score for clean, warning-free Rust with genuine Builder and Strategy patterns and a borrowed zero-copy join. Zero real-data credit because the two datasets are invented and the named source does not exist on Open Baltimore; token concurrency credit; low stakeholder and run credit because answers are computed over six fictional rows and the dashboard is disconnected mock data; README earns 1 for lacking any build/run/verify steps. Total 46/100, F.
